unlisted_practices: Medical schools should adopt contemporary practice competencies as a dynamic, revisable middle layer between stable education program objectives and course- or clerkship-level objectives.

Medical schools should define an AI contemporary practice competency covering critical evaluation of AI-supported recommendations, recognition of limitations and bias, integration of algorithmic outputs into clinical reasoning, communication of uncertainty with patients, and maintenance of professional judgment.
Medical schools should develop AI-related competencies longitudinally across the curriculum rather than as isolated topics or single sessions.
Medical schools should assess AI-related competencies through observable clinical work, such as entrustable professional activities and workplace-based assessments.
Medical schools should keep education program objectives thematic and durable rather than elevating emerging topics such as AI to program objectives.
Curriculum committees should develop and periodically review contemporary practice competencies using existing curricular governance processes.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/commentary paper proposing contemporary practice competencies (CPCs) as a framework for medical education curricula to address AI and technology-driven change.
